text:
sarah: Hey @miguel — receiving a repro from a customer where the Go SDK streaming decoder sometimes returns a JSON unmarshal error mid-stream. They say it happens when a large JSON object gets split across chunks and the internal scanner appears to reset offsets after a retry.

miguel: Ugh. Can you paste the minimal repro and the go-sdk version they're on? :eyes:

sarah: Payload example attached in the ticket but here's a condensed repro: they stream a single JSON array of objects; between token boundaries the server cuts the chunk so a single object straddles two chunks. With go-sdk v0.4.1 the stream reader emits a chunk with partial JSON then on retry the scanner seems to treat the incoming buffer as a new frame and drops the previous partial, resulting in truncated JSON like `{"id":123,"text":"incomplet`. Parse fails.

andrew: Do they use builtin scanner (bufio.Scan) or a custom streaming decoder? Any retry middleware wrapping the reader?

sarah: Using the SDK's Stream method (Go):
```go
cli := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
stream, err := cli.GenerateStream(ctx, req)
for stream.Scan() {
  chunk := stream.Text()
  // json append/merge logic here
}
if err := stream.Err(); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
```
They said they didn't merge partial tokens, relying on Scan to return complete JSON objects.

miguel: That matches. Go's bufio.Scanner has token-size limits and isn't safe for arbitrary fragmentation. We added a custom scanner in 0.5.x to handle chunk reassembly and keep state across retries. If they're on 0.4.1 they might hit this. Ask for the exact server side chunk boundaries (hex offsets) and the client logs.

sarah: I've requested tcpdump and sdk logs. Meanwhile customer provided an example log line: `stream: read 4096 bytes; frame ends at 3900; last token partial -> retry start; scanner offset reset to 0` then `json: unexpected end of JSON input`.

andrew: Two likely causes: 1) SDK retry wrapped the reader and re-exposed only the last partial buffer, losing prefix. 2) The app-level code treats each Scan() result as a full JSON value instead of concatenating into a growing buffer.

miguel: Quick mitigation: upgrade to go-sdk v0.5.2 which switched to a framing-aware low-level reader and removed reliance on bufio.Scanner for token reassembly. If upgrade can't be done, workaround is to buffer chunks yourself and only call json.Unmarshal when you have a complete object. Example minimal merge pattern:
```go
var buf bytes.Buffer
for stream.Scan() {
  buf.WriteString(stream.Text())
  // try decode repeatedly
  dec := json.NewDecoder(&buf)
  for {
    var obj map[string]interface{}
    if err := dec.Decode(&obj); err == io.EOF { break }
    if err != nil { /* not complete yet */ break }
    // process obj
    // After successful decode, reset buf to remaining unread bytes
    rem, _ := io.ReadAll(dec.Buffered())
    buf.Reset()
    buf.Write(rem)
  }
}
```

sarah: Customer says they can't upgrade right now (pinned cluster), asked if there is a config flag they can toggle.

miguel: There's a runtime flag `STREAM_SCAN_TOKEN_LIMIT` and `STREAM_USE_FRAMING` added in 0.5.x but not backported. We can provide a small patch to their pinned version that swaps the scanner implementation; alternatively ship a tiny helper package they can vendor that performs safe reassembly.

andrew: Can you repro locally with the customer's chunking pattern? If so, we can produce a deterministic unit test and offer them a patch/hotfix.

sarah: Repro attached — I was able to reproduce with the following server mock (python):
```py
# sends a JSON object split into 2 chunks at an arbitrary byte offset
data = b'{"id":1,"text":"' + b'a'*2000 + b'"}\n'
sock.send(data[:1200])
time.sleep(0.02)
sock.send(data[1200:])
```
I reproduced failure on 0.4.1, success on 0.5.2.

miguel: Nice. Next steps: 1) create unit test in go-sdk repo that simulates the two-chunk send. 2) Draft patch for 0.4.x (if we decide to backport) that replaces bufio.Scanner usage with a buffer+decoder approach. 3) Provide the customer with the workaround snippet above and an interim binary if they need immediate hotfix.

kate: support-bot posted a follow-up ticket: <https://redwood.support/tickets/INC-5421> — I've linked the repro and requested access to their cluster logs. :white_check_mark:

andrew: Also ask them for the exact go runtime (go1.20 vs go1.21) and whether CGO is enabled. We saw subtle differences in net.Conn buffering when CGO is on.

sarah: Got it — I've asked the customer for go version, tcpdump, and logs. I'll attach the local repro test results showing 0.4.1 vs 0.5.2 behavior. Thanks all. :pray:
